claims.statement: Let f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} be balanced under the uniform measure and let Inf_j(f)=1-epsilon. Put g=x_j f, u=g|_{x_j=+1}, v=g|_{x_j=-1}, let q be the common output bias of u and v, and C=Gamma(1/2). Then H(g)=H(f), I(g)=I(f)-1+2 epsilon, and D_Gamma(f)=(D_Gamma(u)+D_Gamma(v))/2+Gamma(q)-C epsilon-Delta(u,v), where Delta is the exact uniform-selector conditional spectral entropy increment.
hypotheses: f is a finite balanced Boolean function under uniform input
Gamma is a symmetric potential for which the project gate defect is defined

claims.statement: In the same setup, with V_q=4q(1-q) and epsilon<=1/2, Delta(u,v)<=V_q h_2(epsilon/V_q)+(2/ln 2)epsilon. Hence D_Gamma(f)>=avg(D_Gamma(u),D_Gamma(v))+Gamma(q)-(C+2/ln 2)epsilon-V_q h_2(epsilon/V_q). In particular, if both child defects are nonnegative and Gamma(q)>=(C+2/ln 2)epsilon+V_q h_2(epsilon/V_q), then D_Gamma(f)>=0.
hypotheses: for the closure conclusion, D_Gamma(u)>=0 and D_Gamma(v)>=0
claims.rare_event_log_preserved: V_q h_2(epsilon/V_q)=epsilon log_2(V_q/epsilon)+epsilon/ln2+O(epsilon^2/V_q) when epsilon/V_q tends to zero

claims.statement: For the balanced nonempty spectral law P of f with r_j=1-epsilon and nondegenerate I-projection Q_r generated by independent Bernoulli parameters t_i=c r_i conditioned nonempty, define A(T)=P(T union {j})/(1-epsilon), B(T)=P(T)/epsilon on nonempty T, Pi the unconditioned product law on the remaining coordinates, and Pi+ its nonempty conditioning. Then K_occ(f)=(1-epsilon)D_2(A||Pi)+epsilon D_2(B||Pi+). If delta=Pi(nonempty), then delta=c epsilon/(1-c+c epsilon) and D_2(B||Pi)=D_2(B||Pi+)+log_2(1/delta).
hypotheses: nondegenerate I-projection branch mu=sum_i r_i>1; dictator boundary by limit

dependencies.scope: exact conditional-product I-projection Q_r and K_occ definition
